name: Botox versus solifenacin
question: In solifenacin-naïve adults with refractory overactive bladder and urinary incontinence, how do onabotulinumtoxinA and solifenacin compare with placebo?

design.population: Solifenacin-naïve adults with overactive bladder and urinary incontinence after inadequate response to or intolerance of an anticholinergic.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy phase 3b randomized trial
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Purpose and Methods; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Study Overview and Participant Flow

verdictNote: Both active treatments met the placebo comparisons; their direct comparison was post hoc.
takeaway: In solifenacin-naïve patients with refractory overactive bladder, onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U and solifenacin 5–10 mg reduced daily urinary incontinence and increased complete continence versus placebo at 12 weeks; the onabotulinumtoxinA–solifenacin comparison was post hoc.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Herschorn S, Kohan A, Aliotta P, et al. "The Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA or Solifenacin Compared with Placebo in Solifenacin Naïve Patients with Refractory Overactive Bladder: Results from a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind Phase 3b Trial." *J Urol.* 2017;198(1):167-175. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2017.01.069
reports.followUp: Week 12 primary assessment; later open-label onabotulinumtoxinA treatment 2

results.measure: Mean change in daily urinary incontinence episodes from baseline to week 12

effect.p: <0.001 for each active arm versus placebo

results.note: Both active arms met their placebo comparison; direct onabotulinumtoxinA versus solifenacin analysis was post hoc.

results.measure: 100% reduction in daily urinary incontinence episodes at week 12
results.note: The percentages correspond to 49/145, 37/151 and 7/60 in the ClinicalTrials.gov primary outcome table.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Results, primary outcome table

results.measure: Post hoc comparison of week-12 change in daily episodes
results.note: Post hoc direct comparison favored onabotulinumtoxinA.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Results, Adverse Events, urinary tract infection
harms.note: More common with onabotulinumtoxinA; registry safety denominators were 145, 147 and 60 for the three arms.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Results, Adverse Events, urinary retention
harms.note: More common with onabotulinumtoxinA; registry safety denominators were 145, 147 and 60 for the three arms.

delivery.label: Double-dummy initial treatment
delivery.value: Day-1 intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U or saline placebo injection, with daily solifenacin or placebo capsule; solifenacin started at 5 mg and could increase to 10 mg at week 6.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Study Plan, Arms and Interventions

delivery.label: Open-label second treatment
delivery.value: Eligible patients could request open-label onabotulinumtoxinA as treatment 2 after at least 12 weeks.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01767519, Study Plan, Arms and Interventions
